new_skills.name: Number Systems
new_skills.naming_ruling: DEFECT -- near-duplicate, but the analyst's recommended remedy of merging is worse than the defect, so the ruling is: create the node, but not under this name unqualified, and escalate before promotion. Two collisions exist in the 96-name vocabulary. (1) "Number Bases" (line 127) is the narrow base-conversion skill; in CS-flavoured material "number systems" is the standard title for exactly that topic, so two learner-facing labels will read as the same thing while covering different content. The new node's scope must be documented as explicitly EXCLUDING base conversion, which "Number Bases" already owns. (2) "NumberTheory" (line 128) is the more serious overlap: divisibility, primes, factorial prime-counting and remainders are precisely what a NumberTheory node covers, and this is the duplication pattern the 2026-09-08 merge of 48 duplicate names was meant to end. HOWEVER, do NOT resolve it by mapping Number Systems onto NumberTheory. NumberTheory is used in the existing graph as an upstream FOUNDATION node -- "Basic Operations (+, -, x, /) REQUIRES NumberTheory", "Fractions and Decimals REQUIRES NumberTheory", "Modular Arithmetic REQUIRES NumberTheory", "Polynomials and Factoring REQUIRES NumberTheory", "Urdhva Tiryagbhyam REQUIRES NumberTheory". Merging would put 612 advanced CAT questions (157! by 18^n) upstream of Fractions and Decimals, and it would create a hard cycle: the upheld edge becomes NumberTheory -> Prime Numbers, and the graph already contains Prime Numbers -> Basic Operations and Basic Operations -> NumberTheory, closing NumberTheory -> Prime Numbers -> Basic Operations -> NumberTheory. So: create_new_skill=true is correct, topic="CAT Quant" is correct, maps_to_existing_skill=null is correct. The bare name "Number Systems" is the defect. Give the node a name that cannot be confused with either neighbour (the display label should make the exam chapter explicit) and record in the taxonomy memory that NumberTheory is a foundation node, not the chapter node, so the next pass does not re-merge them.

new_skills.name: Geometry and Mensuration
new_skills.naming_ruling: REJECT create_new_skill=true. "Geometry and Mensuration" is a near-duplicate — in fact a portmanteau — of TWO entries already in EXISTING_SKILL_VOCABULARY: "Geometry" and "Mensuration (Area/Volume)". This is precisely the defect the 2026-09-08 vocabulary merge (48 duplicate names collapsed, :Skill 470 to 422) was run to remove, and creating it re-opens that wound. Three independent confirmations: (1) the proposed dependency signature nearly reproduces an existing node's — "Mensuration (Area/Volume) REQUIRES Triangles" and "REQUIRES Circles" already exist, so the new node would sit beside an old node with the same parents; (2) the name is a chapter heading ("Ch 11: Geometry and Mensuration" from arun_sharma_quant), not a skill — it names where the questions were printed, not what a learner must know, and chapter-shaped nodes are unusable for BKT because mastery of "Geometry and Mensuration" is not one latent trait; (3) the sample contradicts the name — nine of fourteen items are polygon angle/diagonal facts and five are triangle theory, while ZERO are mensuration in the "Area/Volume" sense (no solids, no volumes; q10's triangle area is the lone area item). Recommendation: do not mint this node. Route the 422 questions to the existing skills the evidence names — "Polygon Properties" (q0-q8), "Triangles" (q9-q13), "Circles" (q12), "Mensuration (Area/Volume)" (q10) — and if a container is genuinely needed for the chapter, attach it to the existing "Geometry" skill or carry it as a topic/chapter attribute rather than as a new :Skill. Note that if the node is minted anyway, the upheld edges above still stand as written and the maps_to_existing_skill=null in the input file is wrong: it should read "Geometry".
